rationale: The reviewer found that the random pair split leaves every test protein in training, and that labels track per-protein propensity. They measured that all 140 test pairs share proteins with training and that a per-protein label-rate baseline reaches AUROC 0.795, close to the key's ~0.77, and they proposed protein-disjoint splits plus a degree-only baseline. Their other points (small sample, weak negatives, missing controls) are generic or unsupported by the data and don't count as distinct, important issues.
